title: EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path() does not open scene when called on ready
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7-stable, 4.7-rc1, 4.7-beta3, 4.7-beta2
- Not reproducible in 4.5.2-stable, 4.6.3-stable, 4.7-beta1

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (nvidia; 595.71.05) - AMD Ryzen 7 8700F 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.93 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Calling `EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path()` in GDScript will not open the given scene.

I launch the Godot Editor headlessly with various tool-script scenes in order to run build pipeline steps. I need to be able to open extra scenes, modify them, and then close them again. However, after upgrading from 4.5.2 to 4.7, `EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path()` no longer opens scenes.

Here is an example script. I also attached the MRP project.
```gdscript
@tool
extends Node

## To launch from command-line:
## godot --editor --headless res://open_scene.tscn

@export_file_path("*.tscn") var other_scene: String = "res://scene_to_open.tscn"

func _ready():
	# We can have one scene (the scene we started from command-line),
	# to as many scenes as were last open in the Editor.
	print("Startup, open scenes: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scenes())
	print("Startup, open scene roots: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scene_roots())
	print("Startup, edited scene root: ", EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root())

	# We open one scene. In 4.5, the editor would automatically switch to this as the edited scene.
	print("Opening scene ", other_scene)
	EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path(other_scene)

	# In 4.7, no extra scene is opened, and our edited scene root is still the old one.
	print("After opening, open scenes: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scenes())
	print("After opening, open scene roots: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scene_roots())
	print("After opening, edited scene root: ", EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root())
	
	if DisplayServer.window_can_draw():
		print("Not headless, skipping scene closure.")
		return

	# Because no scene was opened, it closes the current one.
	print("Closing currently open scene")
	EditorInterface.close_scene() # This ends up freeing the scene running this script.

	# Script continues running anyway
	print("After closing, edited scene root: ", EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root())
	print("After closing, open scenes: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scenes())
	print("After closing, open scene roots: ", EditorInterface.get_open_scene_roots())
	get_tree().quit() # Fails from calling "get_tree()" on freed instance.
```

Here's how I run it, and resulting output:
```
[alan@virtuoso open_scene_from_path]$ godot --editor --headless res://open_scene.tscn

SCRIPT ERROR: Cannot call method 'get_tree' on a previously freed instance.
          at: _ready (res://open_scene.gd:37)
          GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
              [0] _ready (res://open_scene.gd:37)

```

I would expect there to not be a script error, and for Godot Engine to close without problem after running the script.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Extract example project
2. Inside project directory, run `$ godot --editor --headless res://open_scene.tscn`
3. Script will attempt to open a new editor scene, then immediately close it, but the scene is not opened, so it closes the scene running the script, causing it to be freed and emitting an Script Error

You can also open the scene `res://open_scene.tscn` in the graphical editor. While the code will run, no extra scenes will be opened.
